Job Description: Are you energized by solving complex problems and partnering closely with advisors to bring sophisticated wealth strategies to life? As a Wealth Operations & Complex Case Support Specialist, you will provide high‑touch, end‑to‑end implementation support for large, complex, and multi‑product wealth cases once a client has decided to move forward. This role partners directly with advisors, particularly those without dedicated operations infrastructure to guide them through systems, documentation, and execution complexity. You are A strong execution partner who thrives in complexity and ambiguity and enjoys working directly with advisors and internal teams to drive outcomes. You are known for your ability to translate complicated operational requirements into clear, actionable next steps, and you take pride in seeing sophisticated cases through from post ‑ sale to completion. You are comfortable operating without a script, proactively identifying risks, clarifying ownership, and ensuring momentum in high ‑ stakes, detail ‑ oriented work. You will Lead end-to-end implementation oversight for large, complex, and multi-product wealth cases, ensuring post-sale activity advances through funding, execution, and completion with clear ownership and accountability. Serve as a senior escalation and advisory partner to investment advisers, third-party sponsors, and internal teams, translating complex requirements into practical execution plans and timely next steps. Provide high-touch guidance across required processes, systems, documentation, account structures, sequencing, and dependencies while reinforcing advisor ownership and avoiding duplication of existing responsibilities. Coordinate cross-functional execution with Business Development, Service, Trading Operations, Compliance, Licensing, clearing partners, custodians, and platform sponsors to resolve barriers and maintain momentum on priority cases. Evaluate operational risk, handoffs, escalation points, and process gaps; proactively recommend solutions that reduce advisor friction, improve client delivery, and strengthen controls. Develop and support training, reference materials, and process guidance for relevant products, platforms, and workflows to build field and internal partner capability. Contribute to pilot programs and evolving service models by identifying implementation themes, documenting lessons learned, and supporting scalable improvements for complex-case support. Job Description: Principal Accountabilities: The Senior FP&A Analyst will own the end-to-end consolidated expense reporting process across business areas and shared services. The role is responsible for delivering accurate, timely, and decision-focused reporting; interpreting financial performance; and partnering regularly with finance and business leaders to explain results, challenge assumptions, and support informed decisions. Success requires strong analytical judgment, advanced Excel capability, executive-ready presentation skills, attention to detail, and the confidence to communicate complex financial information clearly. Key Responsibilities: Lead the monthly, quarterly, forecast, and annual consolidated expense reporting cycles, ensuring accurate and timely delivery. Consolidate financial results across business areas, functions, and shared services, with clear reconciliation and control checks. Perform detailed actual-versus-plan, forecast, and prior-year analysis; identify key drivers, trends, risks, and opportunities. Translate complex financial data into concise, actionable commentary and recommendations for senior leadership. Build strong relationships with finance and business leaders through regular reviews, follow-ups, and proactive communication. Own leadership reporting packages, dashboards, and presentations, ensuring a clear story, consistent messaging, and high-quality visuals. Develop and maintain advanced Excel models, reporting templates, reconciliations, and automated controls to improve efficiency and accuracy. Support budgeting, rolling forecasts, scenario analysis, and ad hoc financial requests across multiple stakeholders. Validate data from Oracle, Smart View, or other ERP and planning systems; investigate and resolve discrepancies promptly. Maintain robust governance, documentation, and compliance with internal controls and corporate policies. Identify opportunities to standardize and automate reporting processes while improving the quality of financial insights. Skills & Competencies: Analytical capability: Strong ability to interpret large and complex datasets, connect operational and financial drivers, and develop actionable insights. Advanced Excel: Hands-on expertise with PivotTables, XLOOKUP/INDEX-MATCH, SUMIFS, dynamic formulas, data validation, charts, Power Query, and macros or VBA; ability to build scalable financial models and reporting tools. Executive communication: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to present results, answer questions, and influence senior leaders. Presentation expertise: Strong PowerPoint capability and experience developing executive-ready decks that clearly communicate insights, risks, and recommendations. Business partnership: Ability to build credibility, manage multiple stakeholders, challenge assumptions constructively, and drive timely actions. Financial acumen: Strong understanding of expense management, budgeting, forecasting, month-end close, accruals, allocations, and management reporting. Systems: Experience with Oracle, Smart View, EPBCS/EPM, SAP, Power BI, or comparable ERP, planning, and visualization tools is preferred. Execution: Highly organized, detail-oriented, and able to work independently under tight deadlines while maintaining accuracy and control. Position Summary: The Senior Analyst provides enterprise-level FP&A support through consolidated expense reporting , forecasting , variance analysis, and leadership reporting. Acting as a trusted finance partner, the analyst works closely with leaders across functions to explain performance, identify emerging risks and opportunities, and recommend actions. The role combines strong financial judgment with advanced Excel modeling and executive presentation skills to deliver accurate, insightful, and decision-ready information. Candidate Responsibilities: Take end-to-end ownership of consolidated expense reporting, from data collection and validation through analysis and commentary. Coordinate regularly with finance leaders and business stakeholders to obtain inputs, validate assumptions, resolve issues, and communicate outcomes. Prepare rolling forecasts, budgets, and business plans supported by driver-based analysis and well-reasoned assumptions. Provide comprehensive analysis of current and historical financial performance, including expense, headcount, allocation, and run-rate trends. Create high-quality Excel reports and executive presentations that clearly explain the financial story and required management actions. Manage escalations proactively, investigate reporting issues, and ensure stakeholder questions are addressed accurately and promptly. Functional Skills: Proven ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver high-quality work within month-end and leadership reporting timelines. Strong business partnering and stakeholder-management skills, including frequent interaction with senior leaders. Advanced analytical and problem-solving capability, with a focus on identifying the “why” behind financial results. Exceptional Excel and financial-modeling skills; experience improving or automating complex reporting workbooks. Strong PowerPoint and presentation skills, with the ability to structure messages for executive audiences. Clear, concise written and verbal communication, including variance commentary and leadership discussions. Strong ownership, sound judgment, curiosity, and willingness to challenge data and assumptions constructively. Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across a global, cross-functional environment. Position Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, or a related discipline; MBA, or equivalent qualification is preferred. 5–7 years of progressive FP&A, management reporting, or related finance experience, including consolidated expense reporting and variance analysis. Demonstrated experience partnering with and presenting financial results to senior finance and business leaders. Advanced Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint proficiency is required, supported by practical experience building complex models, reports, and executive presentations. Strong knowledge of expense planning, forecasting, accruals, allocations, general ledger concepts, and management accounting. Experience with Oracle, Smart View, EPM/EPBCS,  or similar financial systems is preferred. Ability to work across time zones, meet tight deadlines, and maintain accuracy in a fast-paced reporting environment. Experience managing internal teams, external partners, vendors, and distributed resources within a matrixed environment. Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively across sales, client management, operations, technology, marketing, product, and service organizations to deliver business impact. Job Description: Guardian's Group Benefits Client Management team is hiring a Client Manager Associate! The Client Manager Associate, Premier Market will assume overall responsibility for managing a client book of business in the 2-99 life space. They will be responsible for persistency, growth, and profitability of this book through relationship development with clients, brokers, and key Guardian internal partners. These partners include Underwriting, Sales Support, Service and Claims. This position will also directly work with Sales Representatives to uncover opportunities to add additional lines of coverage to existing business. This position requires the individual to be an ambassador to the business and always use best practices. The Client Manager Associate is directly and/or indirectly accountable for activities associated with renewing plans (plan retention) and adding new lines of coverage (“add issue”) including, but not limited to, generating plan options and quotes for additional lines of coverage. The individual will proactively evaluate their existing book of business for add issue opportunities, as well as handle incoming renewal and negotiation requests. A successful candidate must demonstrate strong customer service acumen, strong consulting/negotiation skills, deep ancillary product knowledge (dental, vision, life, accident, disability, statutory, supplemental health, voluntary benefits, and leave management) with a high degree of operational effectiveness. You will: Build relationships with brokers/producers/plan holders for groups with less than 100 enrolled lives. Interpret, deliver, and clearly communicate renewals, alternative plan options, and add issue quotes to the broker/producer/client. Review experience and utilization reports with Sales Reps for groups with under 100 lives; Package and deliver appropriate reports based on group size and availability. Proactively identify add issue opportunities for groups under 100 lives by utilizing Salesforce Reports and other strategies developed in collaboration with Sales Reps and generating quotes. Follow up with broker/producer regarding status of renewals and add issue quotes while also engaging the Sales Rep, as needed, to help close the renewal or sale. Provide renewal rate relief for groups under 100 lives through negotiations with underwriting, as well as determining and generating plan alternative options. Serve as subject matter expert on various Guardian systems, capabilities, products, and workflow procedures. You have: Excellent written and oral communication skills Excellent customer service soft skills Very strong mathematical aptitude and analytical skills Strong consultative, negotiation, persuasion, and influencing skills with a sales orientation Ability to build and maintain collaborative working relationships at all levels A client-focused approach Personal accountability Strong planning and organizational skills with ability to multi-task Ability to easily adapt to change Ability to work independently and in a group setting Motivation to meet goals:  Meet persistency goals, renewal target goals, cross-sell goals (add issue), etc. Computer proficiency in Outlook, Skype, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Salesforce, GCRS, Siebel, CPS, Phoenix, Business Objects, etc. Ability to represent Guardian in a professional manner Knowledge: Solid knowledge of group insurance products, contracts, and services. Group insurance products include dental (PPO, DHMO, fully insured and ASO), vision, life, accident, short- and long-term disability (fully insured and ASO), statutory disability, supplemental health, voluntary benefits, and leave management (federal, state, and local). Solid knowledge of financing methodologies and strategies (fully insured and alternate funding) Solid knowledge of group insurance underwriting principles, methodologies, and practices Education: BA or BS Degree is preferred. Will consider work experience equivalent. Experience: 3 to 5 years of insurance industry experience, preferably in a sales environment Demonstrated success in servicing brokers/producers/customers Other: Variable compensation for persistency and renewal target bonus and cross-sell/add-issue bonus, according to the current year Group Sales Incentive Compensation Plan for Client Manager Associates. Must achieve required industry licensing within 90 days of date of hire and maintain license through completing Continuing Education requirements. Job Title: Head of Enterprise Monitoring and Observability
Job Description: Head of Enterprise Monitoring and Observability Reports To Head of Technology Operations Department Enterprise Technology Position Summary The Head of Enterprise Monitoring and Observability is responsible for defining and executing the enterprise observability strategy, operating model, and platform roadmap that enable proactive, predictive, and resilient technology operations. This leader owns the enterprise capabilities for monitoring, telemetry, event intelligence, operational analytics, and observability engineering, ensuring technology services are observable, measurable, actionable, and continuously improving. The role serves as the operational intelligence leader across Enterprise Technology, providing the platforms, standards, insights, and governance required to improve service reliability, accelerate issue detection and resolution, and support modern operational practices. This leader partners closely with infrastructure, cloud, middleware, application, security, resiliency, and service management teams to build a unified enterprise-wide observability capability. Key Responsibilities Enterprise Observability Strategy Define and execute the enterprise observability vision, strategy, operating model, and multi-year roadmap. Establish standards and governance for monitoring, logging, metrics, tracing, telemetry, alerting, and service observability. Lead the evolution of observability capabilities from reactive monitoring toward proactive, predictive, and automated operations. Drive enterprise adoption of modern observability practices, frameworks, and engineering standards. Observability Platform Ownership Own the strategy, architecture, lifecycle, and operation of enterprise monitoring and observability platforms. Lead platform modernization, tool rationalization, capability expansion, and service offering improvements. Manage vendor relationships, contracts, platform investments, and cost optimization efforts. Ensure scalability, availability, resilience, and ongoing enhancement of observability tooling and services. Monitoring and Telemetry Services Establish enterprise monitoring and instrumentation standards across infrastructure, cloud, middleware, applications, databases, and digital services. Improve monitoring coverage, telemetry quality, alert effectiveness, signal quality, and operational visibility. Drive adoption of distributed tracing, service dependency mapping, and end-to-end transaction monitoring. Ensure service health and operational data are consistently available across the technology landscape. Operational Intelligence and AIOps Lead implementation of operational analytics, event intelligence, anomaly detection, predictive insights, and AIOps capabilities. Develop dashboards, scorecards, and reporting that provide actionable operational intelligence to technology leadership. Enable intelligent event correlation, noise reduction, automated diagnostics, and automated operational workflows. Partner with engineering and operations teams to use observability data for continuous improvement and outage prevention. Reliability and Incident Enablement Partner with technology teams to improve detection, response, recovery, and root cause analysis capabilities. Establish observability practices that improve service reliability, operational resilience, and customer experience. Drive post-incident learning and identification of automation opportunities. Provide enterprise visibility into technology health, performance trends, capacity risks, and reliability risks. Leadership and Talent Development Build, lead, and develop a high-performing team of observability engineers, platform engineers, and operational intelligence specialists. Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, operational excellence, continuous learning, and cross-functional partnership. Lead organizational adoption of observability best practices through enablement, coaching, and stakeholder engagement. Establish strong partnerships across technology, cybersecurity, architecture, engineering, operations, resiliency, and service management functions. Qualifications 10+ years of experience in infrastructure operations, platform engineering, observability, reliability engineering, or related technology disciplines. 5+ years of experience leading enterprise-scale engineering or operational teams. Deep expertise in observability platforms, monitoring technologies, telemetry pipelines, logging, metrics, distributed tracing, and operational analytics. Demonstrated experience implementing enterprise monitoring strategies and improving operational reliability at scale. Strong understanding of cloud platforms, hybrid infrastructure, automation, DevOps practices, and modern operational architectures. Experience leading organizational transformation and driving adoption of new operational capabilities. Excellent leadership, communication, stakeholder management, and strategic planning skills. Success Measures Increased enterprise monitoring and observability coverage. Reduced mean time to detect (MTTD) and mean time to resolve (MTTR). Improved signal quality and reduced alert fatigue. Increased adoption of observability standards and platform capabilities. Improved service reliability, operational resilience, and operational efficiency. Expansion of predictive analytics, automation, and AIOps capabilities across Enterprise Technology. Job Description: Company Overview: Every day, Guardian gives 27 million people the security they deserve through our insurance and wealth management products and services. Since our founding in 1860, our long-term view has helped our customers prepare for whatever life brings whether starting a family, planning for the future, or taking care of employees. Today we’re a Fortune 250 company and a leading provider of life, disability and other benefits for individuals, at the workplace and through government sponsored programs. Do you have the desire to be part of a collaborative & innovative technology group? Is a culture where “People Count” and “We do the Right Thing” and “We Hold Ourselves to Very High Standards” important to you? Digital & Technology at Guardian: Digital & Technology (D&T) drives Guardian’s innovation agenda and operational excellence. As a key enabler of Guardian’s Journey to ’30, D&T leverages technology, data, AI, and modern engineering practices to create exceptional customer experiences, support our partners, and empower our colleagues. Through a strong focus on customer-centricity, diversified solutions, expanded reach, and operational excellence, D&T is helping shape the future of how Guardian delivers value across the enterprise. Building the Future of Architecture at Guardian: We're building a high-impact architecture community that will help shape the future of technology at Guardian. Across business-aligned and enterprise architecture roles, our architects influence strategic technology decisions, drive modernization, and help connect business strategy to execution. We are hiring architects across a range of domains—including Group Benefits Technology, FPRS & CSWM Technology, Corporate Functions Technology, Cyber Security, Data, AI, API, Digital, and Enterprise Architecture—and are looking for leaders who can bring strong architectural thinking, technical depth, and the ability to influence across a complex enterprise. Beyond the opportunity to solve challenging business and technology problems, architects joining Guardian today will help define how architecture partners across the organization in the years ahead. You'll collaborate with leaders across engineering, platforms, security, data, AI, and the business to establish standards, guide strategic investments, and create solutions that enable Guardian's long-term success.[JS1] Position Overview: The Principal Enterprise Architect is a senior architecture leader responsible for shaping, guiding, and advancing enterprise architecture across the organization. Reporting to the Head of Enterprise Architecture and Engineering Enablement, this role translates enterprise strategy into practical architecture direction, standards, target-state designs, and transition roadmaps across business capabilities, applications, platforms, data, integration, cloud, security, and emerging technology domains. While architecture is foundational, the Principal Enterprise Architect will be responsible for designing enterprise solutions in close collaboration with the business and technology stakeholders.   Where applicable the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale for the enterprise. This position plays a critical role in connecting enterprise strategy to federated execution. The Principal Enterprise Architect partners with architecture, engineering, platform, security, data, and business technology leaders to ensure material technology decisions align with enterprise standards, target-state architecture, modernization priorities, and governance requirements. This role operates within a federated Enterprise Architecture (EA) model, partnering closely with business technology and platform teams to shape solutions in real time while improving accountability, speed, and delivery alignment. The architect remains connected to the central EA core through enterprise standards, governance, communities of practice, and cross-functional collaboration to ensure consistent, risk-aware technology decisions across domains. The role requires strong strategic thinking, architecture breadth, executive communication, and the ability to influence across a large, complex, and federated enterprise environment. The Principal Enterprise Architect provides architecture leadership and recommendations on material technology decisions and has delegated authority within the enterprise architecture operating model as assigned by the Head of Enterprise Architecture and Engineering Enablement. The role is expected to escalate decisions with enterprise-wide impact, non-standard exceptions, or significant risk implications. Key Responsibilities: Enterprise Architecture Leadership ·      Support the Head of Enterprise Architecture in developing and evolving enterprise architecture strategy, principles, standards, and target-state roadmaps. ·      Define and maintain architecture perspectives across business, application, data, integration, cloud, platform, security, and AI-related capabilities as applicable. ·      Own enterprise standards, target state, governance, exceptions, material technology decision frameworks ·      Translate enterprise strategy and target-state direction into practical guidance for domain architecture and engineering teams. ·      Promote alignment across business units, shared services, and technology domains. ·      Where applicable, the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale and algin to business and technology requirements. Strategic Architecture and Transformation ·      Provide architecture leadership for major strategic initiatives, modernization programs, and enterprise-impacting technology decisions. ·      Assess architecture options and recommend solutions that balance business value, cost, risk, resilience, time to market, and long-term maintainability. ·      Support enterprise transformation through simplification, rationalization, modernization, and platform reuse. ·      Identify opportunities to reduce duplication, retire legacy complexity, and improve interoperability across the enterprise. Governance and Decision Support ·      Participate in and support enterprise architecture governance, standards councils, review boards, and strategic decision forums. ·      Evaluate material technology decisions using approved enterprise frameworks, including buy, build, reuse, partner, and retire options. ·      Review architecture proposals for compliance with enterprise standards, target-state architecture, and risk requirements. ·      Support management of architecture exceptions, including rationale, risk analysis, remediation paths, and time-bound approvals. ·      Available for production incidents with major impact to business operations Cross-Functional Partnership ·      Partner with federated domain architects, platform leaders, engineering teams, data and AI teams, security, infrastructure, and business technology leaders to drive alignment. ·      Facilitate resolution of cross-domain design issues, architecture conflicts, and overlapping capability decisions. ·      Act as a trusted advisor to leaders across technology and business-aligned delivery organizations. ·      Ensure architecture direction is understood and applied consistently across federated teams. ·      Works with Business Unit heads and principal solution architects to translate enterprise direction into federated execution. Risk, Security, and Resilience ·      Incorporate cybersecurity, privacy, resilience, recoverability, and regulatory considerations into architecture guidance and recommendations. ·      Partner with risk, security, and compliance stakeholders to ensure technology decisions align with enterprise control requirements. ·      Assess the operational and architectural implications of technology choices in regulated and high-availability environments. Talent and Capability Development ·      Mentor and coach architects and senior technology professionals. ·      Contribute to architecture capability development, communities of practice, and architecture operating model maturity. ·      Support common role expectations, competency models, and quality standards across the architecture function. ·      Promote enterprise-first thinking, sound decision-making, and strong architecture discipline. You Have: Required Qualifications ·      Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or related field. ·      12+ years of progressive experience in enterprise architecture, solution architecture, domain architecture, or senior technology strategy roles. ·      Deep cross-domain expertise spanning applications, integration, data, AI, cloud, security, and platform strategy. ·      Experience supporting or leading architecture for large-scale transformation initiatives in complex enterprise environments. ·      Experience with architecture governance, standards development, target-state planning, and strategic technology decision-making. ·      Proven ability to influence across organizational boundaries without direct authority. ·      Strong written, verbal, and presentation communication skills. Preferred Education and Experience ·      Experience in insurance, financial services, healthcare, or another highly regulated industry. ·      Experience in a federated technology organization with centralized architecture direction and distributed execution. ·      Experience with cloud modernization, API strategies, platform engineering, data ecosystems, and enterprise integration. ·      Familiarity with AI-enabled enterprise capabilities, automation, and emerging technology trends. ·      Advanced degree and/or relevant certifications such as TOGAF, SAFe, AWS, Azure, GCP, or equivalent. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities ·      Strong knowledge of enterprise architecture principles, methods, and governance practices. ·      Broad understanding of enterprise technology domains and cross-domain dependencies. ·      Ability to develop target-state architecture and pragmatic transition approaches. ·      Strong business acumen and ability to connect architecture decisions to business outcomes. ·      Ability to assess tradeoffs among speed, cost, quality, risk, and strategic fit. ·      Strong facilitation, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills. ·      Ability to communicate effectively with executive, business, and technical audiences. ·      Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities. ·      Ability to operate effectively in ambiguity and lead through influence. Job Description: The Manager, Trading Operations & Controls is responsible for leading the firm's trading operations governance, regulatory reporting, and trading control framework across both the Broker-Dealer (BD) and Registered Investment Advisor (RIA) businesses. This role oversees critical trading functions including best execution, trade supervision, trading rules management, regulatory reporting, margin oversight, trade corrections, and order review processes, while ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements and internal policies. The position also leads operational reporting and team governance initiatives, partnering closely with Compliance, Technology, custodial partners, and business stakeholders to drive operational excellence, risk management, and an exceptional advisor and client experience. You will Manage the firm’s Best Execution responsibilities for both the RIA and the BD. This role would be responsible for the firm’s execution of our procedures with regard to Best Ex and be the Relationship Owner with our vendor partner. This would require managing trading desk tasks, reviews, and the compilation of the quarterly scorecards for the Park Avenue committee review. Responsible for managing the firm’s implementation of Pershing’s trading rules system, the Enterprise Rules Engine (ERE). This would require the full understanding and managing of the firm’s approved products, how systems integrate and can be leveraged with the ERE, interact with the Compliance team for approval of changes, and fully appreciate the client impacts and suggest custom messages for rules implemented to better educate clients and advisors about why trades are reviewed prior to execution. Primarily responsible for the compliance of the firm's trade related regulatory reporting for all security types, e.g. equity, options, fixed income, alternatives, FX. Manage the trade correction intake, review, approval, and monitoring process for both the RIA and BD business. Manage the margin process for both the RIA and BD business. Manage the firm’s responsibilities with regard to trading in the proprietary portfolios with the Digital RIA, Vestwise. Manage the firm’s trading executions within the Orion system for the separate RIA, Park Avenue Advisory. Manage the firm’s trading house accounts. Create processes around the review and monitoring of the firm’s trade reject account, error account, average price and allocation accounts. Manage the firm’s Review and Release process for equity, fixed income and mutual fund order processing. Manage the firm’s email intake of issues to the group. Metrics – Manage the overall process the larger group uses to collect, manage, and disseminate operational metrics. Manage the process of goal setting (improvement) and monitor the adherence to our goals throughout the year. Administers, develops, communicates, and presents key metrics/reporting to management at all levels. Updates/creates miscellaneous documents for various platforms i.e., meetings, conferences, SLT, etc. Oversee and inspire a high performing team through daily coaching, training, and call/contact listening, providing tailored development feedback to each team member, and driving employee engagement. Proactively monitor schedule adherence and behaviors to ensure team members are in the right place, at the right time, to effectively serve our customers. Manage Team Procedures Reviews and Attestations – responsible for ensuring the team has finalized written operational procedures and oversees the regular review and attestation process for all operational teams. You have Required: 5-10 years’ experience in financial services, preferably at a Broker Dealer (BD) or Registered Investment Advisor (RIA) in a trading operations role Outstanding organizational and time management skills Experience managing small teams and processes Minimum of 2-3 years of high touch customer service or operations experience, specifically with strong wealth management trading knowledge and background. Job Title: Head of Product Strategy & Platform Innovation
Job Description: The Head of Product Strategy & Platform Innovation is a senior leadership role responsible for the strategic evolution, differentiation, and commercial success of our open‑architecture wealth management product platform. This individual wakes up every day thinking about what’s next —how product, partners, packaging, and go‑to‑market strategy come together to create a compelling, modern, and advisor‑centric platform across fee‑based advisory, annuities, and alternatives. We do not manufacture products. Our competitive advantage comes from curation, partnership, design, positioning, and delivery . This role exists to ensure our platform is not merely comprehensive—but distinctive, relevant, and growth‑oriented . The role works horizontally across the organization —marketing, sales, business development, training, product management—and externally with asset managers, insurance carriers, TAMPs, and portfolio managers . Success requires influence without direct ownership, entrepreneurial energy, and a strong commercial mindset. Key Responsibilities Product Strategy & Innovation Own the forward‑looking product strategy across advisory, annuities, and alternatives within an open‑architecture ecosystem. Identify gaps, white spaces, and emerging opportunities driven by advisor needs, client behavior, regulation, and competitive dynamics. Design differentiated product constructs, solutions, and portfolios by creatively leveraging third‑party partners rather than manufacturing products. Translate industry trends (e.g., retirement income, tax efficiency, private markets, managed solutions, model portfolios) into actionable platform initiatives. Platform Differentiation & Go‑to‑Market Develop clear go‑to‑market strategies for platform capabilities, including positioning, messaging, and advisor value propositions. Partner closely with Marketing to ensure product stories are simple, compelling, and commercially effective . Work with Sales and Business Development to align product strategy with advisor adoption, growth objectives, and field readiness . Drive clarity around why advisors should use specific solutions—not just what is available. Partner Strategy & Ecosystem Management Serve as a senior point of engagement with asset managers, insurance carriers, TAMPs, and product sponsors . Evaluate, onboard, and rationalize partners with a focus on quality, differentiation, economics, and strategic fit . Co‑create solutions with partners where appropriate, including custom portfolios, white‑labeled offerings, or exclusive access strategies . Maintain a strong commercial lens on platform economics, scalability, and advisor impact. Cross‑Functional Leadership & Influence Act as a strategic connector across Product Management, Sales, Marketing, Training, and Business Development. Provide strategic direction while leveraging existing execution teams for implementation. Influence priorities and outcomes without direct people ownership , using clarity, credibility, and collaboration. Partner with Training and Sales Enablement to ensure advisors understand not just products—but how to use them in holistic planning conversations . What Success Looks Like Advisors view the platform as thoughtful, differentiated, and easy to position with clients . Product initiatives are clearly linked to advisor adoption, client outcomes, and revenue growth . Partners see the firm as a strategic collaborator , not just a distributor. The platform evolves proactively— not reactively —to market and advisor needs. Qualifications & Experience 10+ years of experience in wealth management, asset management, insurance, or fintech, with exposure to RIA and broker‑dealer environments . Deep knowledge of fee‑based advisory, annuities, alternatives, and managed solutions . Demonstrated ability to build or evolve open‑architecture platforms without manufacturing products. Strong commercial and go‑to‑market orientation —understands how strategy translates into advisor behavior. Proven success working cross‑functionally and influencing outcomes without direct authority. Entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to balance vision with practical execution . Comfortable operating with ambiguity and turning ideas into scalable initiatives. Why This Role Matters This role ensures our product platform moves from “robust but pedestrian” to strategically curated, commercially sharp, and advisor‑obsessed —without disrupting what already works operationally. It complements strong execution with vision, innovation, and market leadership . Manage a high-volume workload while prioritizing customer needs, resolving issues proactively, and supporting continuous quality improvement initiatives. Job Description: STD/Absence Claims Case Manager I Job Description Revised August 2026 The STD/Absence Claims Case Manager I (CM) is responsible for adjudicating and medically managing Short Term and Absence claims involving specific diagnoses or leave types that tend to resolve quickly. The CM will work with employers, employees, and health care providers to administer Short Term disability in conjunction with other paid or unpaid leaves covered by Guardian, including Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA), State Paid Medical Leave, and/or State Paid Disability. The CM will manage the claim according to the plan provisions, state and federal guidelines, and established protocols. This role requires sound judgment, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills to work independently, interpret contract provisions, analyze medical and claim information, and administer benefits through the appropriate claim duration or return to work. The CM is responsible for meeting key service deliverables such as turnaround times, quality assurance, and overall customer experience. This position utilizes analytical reasoning, problem solving, adaptability, and strong written and verbal communication skills to ensure timely and appropriate absence and disability claim decisions while providing superior customer service to all internal and external customers. This position requires consistent and effective claim management skills, resilience in a fast-paced environment, and the ability to adapt as claim circumstances, priorities, or information change. Candidate Responsibilities Effectively understand contract language and plan design for group disability Communicate claim status and decisions via telephone and in writing Initiate communications to claimant, physician, and planholder to assess and facilitate job accommodation opportunities Proactive outreaches to claimants, planholders, and physicians via telephone for information needed for initial and ongoing claim management (e.g. current earnings, other income benefits, medical information, etc.); notifies claimants when claims are pended for missing information Proactively identify claim issues, develop and execute a well-reasoned plan of action for pending and ongoing disability claims, and adjust strategies as new information becomes available. Utilize, manage, and direct appropriate resources to support timely and accurate benefit determination for internal and external customers in accordance with policy provisions, regulatory requirements, internal standards, and customer service expectations. Apply critical thinking to investigate, analyze, and synthesize claim information, contract provisions, medical documentation, and regulatory requirements to determine coverage, benefit eligibility, and appropriate claim outcomes. Demonstrate adaptability and resilience by effectively managing shifting priorities, changing claim circumstances, and time-sensitive decisions in a fast-paced environment. Determine if claimants meet the definition of disability as defined in the contract by reviewing occupational requirements, analyzing medical information, identifying gaps or inconsistencies, and applying sound judgment to reach appropriate claim decisions. Review, validate, and refine AI-generated claim recommendations, data extractions, and draft correspondence, applying professional judgment before finalizing decisions or communications. Verify the accuracy and completeness of AI-assembled claim files and AI-flagged discrepancies, ensuring quality, regulatory compliance, and audit-readiness of claim documentation. Establish, document and execute claim action plan and recommended path including return to active work at claimant’s own job Determine Insured Earnings by reviewing payroll information from the planholder and calculate payable benefits according to plan provisions, with strong attention to accuracy, detail, and applicable offsets. Follow all claim management procedures and facilitate potential return to work and job accommodation opportunities when applicable Utilize claim management resources such as MDA (Medical Disability Guidelines) and other disability tools to assist with appropriate durational disability Assess claim when other sources of income are received (e.g., social security, state disability, etc.,) to ensure accurate offsets are applied and recalculate benefits, as needed, to determine under/overpayments.   Proactively work with claimants to recover overpayments in full or negotiate monthly installments according to established protocols Assess claim for restrictions and limitations to establish appropriate partnership with PRT Remain composed, resourceful, and solutions-oriented when resolving routine claim challenges, addressing missing information, and determining appropriate next steps. Job Title: Head of Data Engineering, Corporate & Enterprise
Job Description: Position Overview: The Head of Data Engineering, Corp & Enterprise is a mid- leadership role accountable for the end-to-end data engineering lifecycle across Guardian's Corporate and business unit and Enterprise, from source data acquisition, ingestion, and transformation through the delivery of trusted, production-ready data products that power AI, machine learning, reporting, analytics, and business applications. This leader owns the strategy, architecture direction, engineering execution, and operational health of the data supply chain that downstream teams depend on every day. This is a player-coach role. The Head of Data Engineering leads a team of US FTEs and provides direction to an extended indirect engineering team in India, building a high-performing, globally distributed delivery model with clear standards, strong engineering discipline, and a culture of ownership. While the role is primarily a leadership position, the leader is expected to stay technically current and go hands-on when needed reviewing designs, unblocking complex engineering problems, and setting the bar for quality through example. A core mandate of this role is ownership and maturing Guardian's Master Data Management (MDM) practice. Job Description: The Planning Team Leader for Guardian Wealth Partners (GWP) is a strategic leadership role responsible for building, leading, and scaling a high-performing advisor team within Guardian’s fee-based Registered Investment Advisor platform. In addition to overseeing the GWP Planning team and client delivery, this leader will play a critical role in developing and executing the client acquisition go-to-market strategy for Guardian Wealth Partners, including target client segments, referral pathways, distribution partnerships, and scalable engagement models. This individual will own the end-to-end acquisition, growth and retention strategy for prospects and clients originating from other Guardian business lines, with accountability for converting qualified opportunities into long-term advisory relationships, delivering differentiated client experience, and building servicing models that support retention, and deeper engagement. The role will partner closely with Group Distribution and other enterprise stakeholders to build the Guardian Wealth Partners practice, strengthen connectivity across business lines, and ensure the offering is positioned as a compelling wealth management solution for clients across different targeted segmentations ranging from mass affluent to high net worth through a combination of fully digital and hybrid engagement models. Key Responsibilities Sales & Growth Leadership Lead and develop a team of (centralized/in-house) advisors responsible for converting inbound leads into long‑term advisory relationships. Define and execute the client acquisition go-to-market strategy for Guardian Wealth Partners, including client segmentation, channel prioritization, referral source development, advisor coverage models, and conversion strategies. Develop segmented servicing models that align client needs, complexity, and relationship value with the appropriate combination of digital, hybrid, and advisor-led engagement. Drive growth across subscription‑based planning, fee‑based financial planning, and fee‑based investment management offerings. Build the operating rhythm, metrics, and feedback loops needed to evaluate go-to-market effectiveness, including lead quality, conversion rates, advisor productivity, client acquisition cost, revenue growth, and client outcomes. Serve as a strategic partner to senior leaders across Distribution, Wealth Management, Product, Marketing, Operations, and Compliance to support the continued growth and maturation of the Guardian Wealth Partners practice. Client Journey & Experience Design and oversee the servicing and retention strategy for Guardian Wealth Partners clients, ensuring clients receive consistent, high-quality experience from initial engagement through onboarding, planning, implementation, and ongoing relationship management. Ensure a consistent experience across digital planning tools, fully digital workflows, and hybrid advisor‑led engagements. Champion a client‑centric, education‑driven approach that builds trust, clarity, and long‑term partnerships with clients. Ensure advice delivery is aligned with fiduciary standards and the firm’s holistic planning philosophy. Establish proactive client engagement standards, including ongoing planning reviews, education touchpoints, relationship deepening opportunities, and service escalation protocols. Monitor client experience, retention indicators, and service quality to identify opportunities for continuous improvement and ensure the practice delivers on its client promise. Collaborate with Group Distribution leaders and Field Leaders to identify market opportunities, clarify referral expectations, improve handoff processes, and create consistent field engagement strategies. Create mechanisms for ongoing feedback between Guardian Wealth Partners advisors, Group Distribution and Field partners to improve lead quality, client readiness, and conversion outcomes. Advisor Management & Development Recruit, onboard, coach, and develop a high‑performing team of advisors. Set clear performance expectations, sales goals, and activity metrics aligned with firm objectives. Develop a way to track performance/activity metrics and goals to utilize as coaching and share with senior leadership. Foster a strong sales and advice culture focused on collaboration, professionalism, and continuous improvement. Support advisors through training and coaching in building consultative skills across planning, education, and investment implementation. Required Licenses/Education Series 65/66 Bachelor’s degree Preferred Licenses/Education Advanced degree and/or CFP®, CFA®, or similar credentials preferred Required Experience 10+ years of experience in wealth management, advisory sales, or financial planning, with at least 5 years in a leadership role Deep understanding of fee‑based advisory models, holistic financial planning, and investment management Experience leading advisor teams across multiple client segments, including affluent and HNW Demonstrated experience developing and executing client acquisition, go-to-market, or distribution partnership strategies within wealth management, financial planning, advisory sales, or a related financial services environment. Proven ability to scale sales organizations using digital and hybrid engagement models Strong working knowledge of RIA regulatory and fiduciary standards Proven ability to build and scale servicing and retention models that improve client engagement, deepen relationships, and support long-term business growth. Experience partnering with field distribution, sales leadership, or enterprise channels to build referral strategies, improve lead conversion, and drive practice growth. Strong strategic orientation with the ability to translate business objectives into clear operating plans, performance metrics, advisor routines, and client experience improvements. We drive a high-performance culture across our Legal, Compliance, and Government Affairs functions, aligned to “what” we deliver (i.e., our goals and objectives) and “how” we demonstrate our values and behaviors while focusing on the customer. We do this through leveraging a series of core capabilities, which includes accountability, interpersonal effectiveness, ability to demonstrate business savvy, being a subject matter expert, all while supporting the Law Department’s Mission to be a trusted advocate and advisor to drive strategic solutions that advance Guardian’s purpose, priorities, and values. You will play a critical role in providing legal advice to business partners regarding Guardian’s individual markets business with a particular emphasis on the distribution of individual insurance products, and support for the company’s broker/dealer and registered investment adviser as well as supporting its advanced markets team. A successful candidate will have excellent research and organizational skills, and business judgment as you will be required to understand and manage the laws and regulations affecting individual insurance products and wealth management offerings and provide practical advice in a rapidly changing and high-profile regulatory environment. You will also need to draft applicable agreements with distribution partners and help to facilitate the succession of general agencies. The ability to influence and drive proactive partnership in a changing business environment is critical. You will develop cross-business connections, provide industry perspective and best practices guidance while considering long-term outcomes and the needs of partners/clients when providing advice. You are Energized and excited by challenging goals; and reflected in a true sense of competitiveness and drive for results. Adaptable. You embrace ambiguity, complexity, uncertainty, and volatility. A strategic problem solver able to simplify strategic success and innovation. An effective communicator, with a proven record of influencing cross-functional teams establishing and leading strong relationships with critical partners and executive stakeholders. Able to effectively convey ideas and engage in meaningful conversations. You will Provide advice and counsel to CSWM strategies and innovation initiatives in their organizations. Participate in external forums, build partnerships internally across Guardian, and help ensure that Guardian’s CSWM business practices and policies are compliant with applicable law. Advise and assist with the implementation of new distribution and wealth management related laws and regulations. Represent the practice group as a key advisor to stakeholders to establish, inform, and maintain company-wide compliant policies. Provide effective, prompt compliance advice and support business compliance, rectifying problems, and responding to emerging challenges. Keep informed regarding pending industry changes, trends, and best practices and assess the potential impact of these changes on organizational processes. You have 7 – 10 years of experience, preferably in connection with the life insurance and/or wealth management industries. Job Description: Position Overview: The Principal Solution Architect, Data is responsible for defining, scaling, and governing enterprise-wide or business solution architecture across platforms, domains, and delivery teams. This role shapes how technology solutions are designed, integrated, secured, and operated consistently across the organization. While architecture is foundational, the Principal Solution Architect, Data will be responsible for designing solutions in close collaboration with the business and technology stakeholders. Where applicable, the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale and align to business and technology requirements. Operating at an enterprise or portfolio level, the Principal Solution Architect, Data focuses less on individual solution delivery and more on establishing architecture patterns, standards, guardrails, and building solutions that enable teams to deliver high-quality, scalable, and secure solutions at speed. This role operates within a federated Enterprise Architecture (EA) model, partnering closely with business technology and platform teams to shape solutions in real time while improving accountability, speed, and delivery alignment. The architect remains connected to the central EA core through enterprise standards, governance, communities of practice, and cross-functional collaboration to ensure consistent, risk-aware technology decisions across domains. This role partners closely with Enterprise Architecture, Engineering, Product, Cybersecurity, and Platform teams to ensure solutions align to business strategy, are resilient and compliant, and can scale across multiple use cases without becoming a bottleneck to delivery. This Principal Solution Architect, Data role will have a strong focus on data solution architecture, modern data platforms, data products, and AI-enabled capabilities across the Insurance business. The role bridges business, engineering, architecture, and data teams to rapidly design, build, and deploy scalable solutions that improve underwriting, enrollment, billing, claims, customer service, Producer, reporting, analytics, and digital experiences. The architect will champion a data product mindset, treating data as a strategic enterprise asset with clear ownership, quality standards, reusable capabilities, governance, and measurable customer value. Key Responsibilities: Own and shape enterprise or business solution architecture strategy, standards, and patterns across multiple platforms and domains. Define and maintain reference architectures and reusable design patterns (“golden paths”) for solution delivery. Establish architectural guardrails that enable scalable, secure, and consistent solution design across teams. Own reusable solution patterns, reference architectures, golden paths, and cross-team design consistency. Work with Solution Architects to drive adoption; Head of Portfolio Architecture to tailor for BU context; Principal Enterprise Architect to align with enterprise standards. Lead enterprise-level or business-level design decisions for complex, high-impact initiatives that span multiple value streams or business units. Provide architectural oversight and guidance across portfolios, ensuring alignment to enterprise standards and long-term strategy. Drive early engagement on initiatives to identify cross-platform dependencies, systemic risks, and scalability constraints. Partner with Enterprise Architecture and platform teams to define build vs. buy guidance and integration patterns. Translate business and technology strategy into actionable architecture direction and solution designs. Partner with Security, Risk, and Compliance teams to embed governance, security, and regulatory requirements into solution architecture. Define and promote best practices for operational resilience, scalability, performance, and maintainability. Escalate enterprise exceptions, non-standard patterns, and enterprise-risk decisions. Influence and align stakeholders across engineering, product, and business leadership without direct authority. Mentor and coach architects and senior engineers to elevate architectural maturity across the organization. Represent solution architecture in enterprise forums, architecture review boards, and strategic technology discussions. Influence Value Stream leaders, Product Managers, Product Owners, and Tech Leads to align roadmaps, MVP scope, and technical trade-offs. Where applicable, the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale and algin to business and technology requirements. Be available for production incidents with major impact to business operations. Job Description: Principal Solution Architect, Enterprise API Platform Position Overview: The Principal Solution Architect, Enterprise API Platform, is responsible for defining, scaling, and governing enterprise-wide or business solution architecture across platforms, domains, and delivery teams. This role shapes how technology solutions are designed, integrated, secured, and operated consistently across the organization. While architecture is foundational, the Principal Solution Architect will be responsible for designing solutions in close collaboration with the business and technology stakeholders.   Where applicable, the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale and algin to business and technology requirements. Operating at an enterprise or portfolio level, the Principal Solution Architect focuses less on individual solution delivery and more on establishing architecture patterns, standards, guardrails and building solutions that enable teams to deliver high-quality, scalable, and secure solutions at speed. This role operates within a federated Enterprise Architecture (EA) model, partnering closely with business technology and platform teams to shape solutions in real time while improving accountability, speed, and delivery alignment. The architect remains connected to the central EA core through enterprise standards, governance, communities of practice, and cross-functional collaboration to ensure consistent, risk-aware technology decisions across domains. This role partners closely with Enterprise Architecture, Engineering, Product, Cybersecurity, and Platform teams to ensure solutions align to business strategy, are resilient and compliant, and can scale across multiple use cases—without becoming a bottleneck to delivery. For the Enterprise API Platform, this role serves as the strategic and technical architecture partner to the Head of Enterprise API Platform, helping translate API modernization and transformation objectives into practical, value-generating modernization decisions, reusable architecture patterns, MCP-enabled platform direction, and executable engineering outcomes. You Will (Key Responsibilities): Own and shape enterprise or business solution architecture strategy, standards, and patterns across multiple platforms and domains Define and maintain reference architectures and reusable design patterns (“golden paths”) for solution delivery Establish architectural guardrails that enable scalable, secure, and consistent solution design across teams Owns reusable solution patterns, reference architectures, golden paths, and cross-team design consistency Work with Solution Architects to drive adoption; Head of Portfolio Architecture to tailor for BU context; Principal Enterprise Architect to align with enterprise standards Lead enterprise-level or business-level design decisions for complex, high-impact initiatives that span multiple value streams or business units Provide architectural oversight and guidance across portfolios, ensuring alignment to enterprise standards and long-term strategy Drive early engagement on initiatives to identify cross-platform dependencies, systemic risks, and scalability constraints Partner with Enterprise Architecture and platform teams to define build vs. buy guidance and integration patterns Translate business and technology strategy into actionable architecture direction and solution designs Partner with Security, Risk, and Compliance teams to embed governance, security, and regulatory requirements into solution architecture Define and promote best practices for operational resilience, scalability, performance, and maintainability Escalate enterprise exceptions / non-standard patterns / enterprise-risk decisions Influence and align stakeholders across engineering, product, and business leadership without direct authority Mentor and coach architects and senior engineers to elevate architectural maturity across the organization Represent solution architecture in enterprise forums, architecture review boards, and strategic technology discussions Influences Value Stream leaders, Product managers, Product Owners and Tech Leads to align roadmaps, MVP scope, and technical trade-offs. Where applicable, the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale and algin to business and technology requirements. Available for production incidents with major impact to business operations Balance strategic and tactical decisions across API modernization, API/MCP management, API lifecycle management, domain-aligned data models, reimplementation priorities, and AI-ready API capabilities. Continuously evaluate now versus later, strategic versus tactical, reusable versus disposable, and modernization versus value delivery, ensuring meaningful outcomes through thin slices rather than broad, low-value transformation efforts. Lead enterprise API architecture patterns, technical direction, and modernization alignment across API platform engineering, internal API delivery, external API delivery, and high-impact integration initiatives. Drive API rationalization, reuse, and domain alignment by helping teams redesign APIs around business capability-based, domain-aligned data models and solve common problems once rather than repeatedly. Guide reimplementation decisions for APIs coupled to non-performant or non-scalable data sources, balancing resiliency, scalability, maintainability, delivery urgency, and longer-term architectural direction. Help shape Guardian’s API, MCP gateway, and context-layer strategy so APIs become trusted, discoverable, observable, and governed inputs into agentic AI, reusable business capabilities, and future AI-native experiences. Serve as a critical daily and weekly architecture input to the Head of Enterprise API Platform, improving decision quality, decision velocity, modernization sequencing, and executive confidence in API transformation progress. Translate complex API architecture decisions into business outcomes, helping senior technology and business leaders understand “what this means” in terms of value, risk, scalability, execution, AI enablement, and strategic platform direction. Proven ability to define and drive adoption of architecture standards, frameworks, and reusable patterns Strong understanding of modern technology ecosystems (application architectures, APIs and delivery, integration patterns, AI, cloud platforms, and data flows) Experience balancing business priorities, technical trade-offs, and risk at an enterprise level Demonstrated ability to operate at both strategic and hands-on levels when needed Strong experience influencing technical direction across distributed teams without direct reporting authority Ability to bridge business and technology, translating strategy into clear architectural direction Excellent communication skills with the ability to convey complex concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences Experience working in regulated or risk-sensitive environments with strong awareness of governance and compliance needs Track record of mentoring architects and engineers and elevating organizational capabilities Experience collaborating within Agile / product-based delivery models. Experience producing product-level and team-level technical design documentation. Strong engineering background with the ability to operate as a credible technical partner to engineering leaders while also shaping enterprise-level API architecture strategy. Demonstrated ability to balance pragmatic delivery with disruptive architectural thinking, including sequencing modernization work around prioritized strategic initiatives, high-visibility outcomes, and critical high-transaction-volume integrations. Strong understanding of MCP, agentic AI enablement, context-layer architecture, API observability, discoverability, governance, security, and the role of APIs as foundational inputs into AI-native enterprise capabilities. You will: You will collaborate closely with cross-functional teams, stakeholders, and technology partners to develop and integrate automation solutions that drive business growth, improve customer experiences, and reduce operational costs. You have: Bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, engineering, management or a related field. Strong people leadership experience managing software engineering teams, including hiring, coaching, performance management, and developing senior technical talent. Deep hands-on technical background designing, building, and operating production-grade distributed systems, AI/ML platforms, data platforms, or cloud-native runtime services. Experience leading teams responsible for the execution layer of a platform, including runtime services, model inference, retrieval, orchestration, tool invocation, workflow execution, or production AI operations. Ability to own the roadmap and delivery for execution plane capabilities such as model gateways, agent runtimes, tool/action gateways, runtime adapters, MCP services, knowledge bases, retrieval pipelines, inference services, and deployment patterns. Strong understanding of data access patterns, enterprise APIs, retrieval-augmented generation, embeddings, vector/search systems, context engineering, and governed access to systems of record. Experience building reliable, scalable, low-latency execution services with clear contracts, strong observability, graceful degradation, retry patterns, rate limits, and operational resilience. Ability to partner with control plane, developer experience, data engineering, security, architecture, operations, and domain application teams to ensure execution technologies operate behind governed platform interfaces. Proven ability to drive engineering excellence through design reviews, architecture standards, testing, CI/CD, infrastructure automation, incident response, SLOs, runbooks, and production support mechanisms. Strong understanding of enterprise security and compliance requirements for runtime execution, including identity propagation, auditability, data handling, least privilege access, secrets management, and environment isolation. Strong communication and influence skills, with the ability to simplify complex runtime, data, and AI execution topics for senior stakeholders while aligning teams around reusable platform patterns. You will: Experience with agentic AI systems, LLM platforms, model gateways, agent runtimes, tool/action gateways, MCP servers, orchestration frameworks, or AI execution engines. Experience with AWS-based AI execution services and cloud-native patterns, including Bedrock, AgentCore, SageMaker, Lambda, Step Functions, API Gateway, EKS, DynamoDB, S3, IAM, CloudWatch, and related DevOps tooling. Familiarity with RAG systems, enterprise search, vector databases, embedding models, rerankers, knowledge bases, context engineering, and governed retrieval from enterprise data sources. Experience designing multi-tenant runtime platforms with environment isolation, workload identities, RBAC/ABAC, cross-account access patterns, quotas, throttling, and secure service-to-service communication. Background in MLOps, LLMOps, AIOps, model lifecycle management, evaluation pipelines, model serving, inference optimization, or production AI operations. Experience with observability for AI workloads, including distributed tracing, token usage, latency, model/tool errors, cost attribution, quality metrics, safety metrics, and operational dashboards. Experience with performance, scalability, and cost optimization for high-volume runtime services, including caching, batching, streaming, load testing, capacity planning, and GPU/CPU optimization where applicable. Experience building reusable platform abstractions, SDKs, runtime adapters, reference architectures, or deployment templates that make execution technologies portable across vendors and use cases. Experience integrating enterprise tools, APIs, data services, and workflow systems through governed connectors rather than point-to-point application wiring. Job Description: The Principal Enterprise Architect is a senior architecture leader responsible for shaping, guiding, and advancing enterprise architecture across the organization. Reporting to the Head of Enterprise Architecture and Engineering Enablement , this role translates enterprise strategy into practical architecture direction, standards, target-state designs, and transition roadmaps across business capabilities, applications, platforms, data, integration, cloud, security, and emerging technology domains. While architecture is foundation al, the Principal Enterprise Architect will be responsible for design ing enterprise solutions in close collaboration with the business and technology stakeholders . Where applicable the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale for the enterprise. This position plays a critical role in connecting enterprise strategy to federated execution. The Principal Enterprise Architect partners with architecture, engineering, platform, security, data, and business technology leaders to ensure material technology decisions align with enterprise standards, target-state architecture, modernization priorities, and governance requirements. The role requires strong strategic thinking, architecture breadth, executive communication, and the ability to influence across a large, complex, and federated enterprise environment. The Principal Enterprise Architect provides architecture leadership and recommendations on material technology decisions and has delegated authority within the enterprise architecture operating model as assigned by the Head of Enterprise Architecture. The role is expected to escalate decisions with enterprise-wide impact, non-standard exceptions, or significant risk implications. Key Responsibilities: Enterprise Architecture Leadership Support the Head of Enterprise Architecture in developing and evolving enterprise architecture strategy , principles, standards, and target-state roadmaps. Define and maintain architecture perspectives across business, application, data, integration, cloud, platform, security, and AI-related capabilities as applicable. Own enterprise standards, target state, governance, exceptions, material technology decision frameworks Translate enterprise strategy and target-state direction into practical guidance for domain architecture and engineering teams. Promote alignment across business units, shared services, and technology domains. Strategic Architecture and Transformation Provide architecture leadership for major strategic initiatives, modernization programs, and enterprise-impacting technology decisions. Assess architecture options and recommend solutions that balance business value, cost, risk, resilience, time to market, and long-term maintainability. Support enterprise transformation through simplification, rationalization, modernization, and platform reuse. Identify opportunities to reduce duplication, retire legacy complexity, and improve interoperability across the enterprise. Governance and Decision Support Participate in and support enterprise architecture governance, standards councils, review boards, and strategic decision forums. Evaluate material technology decisions using approved enterprise frameworks, including buy, build, reuse, partner, and retire options. Review architecture proposals for compliance with enterprise standards, target-state architecture, and risk requirements. Support management of architecture exceptions, including rationale, risk analysis, remediation paths, and time-bound approvals. Available for production incidents with major impact to business operations Cross-Functional Partnership Partner with federated domain architects, platform leaders, engineering teams, data and AI teams, security, infrastructure, and business technology leaders to drive alignment. Facilitate resolution of cross-domain design issues, architecture conflicts, and overlapping capability decisions. Act as a trusted advisor to leaders across technology and business-aligned delivery organizations. Ensure architecture direction is understood and applied consistently across federated teams. Works with Business Unit heads and principal solution architects to translate enterprise direction into federated execution. Risk, Security, and Resilience Incorporate cybersecurity, privacy, resilience, recoverability, and regulatory considerations into architecture guidance and recommendations. Partner with risk, security, and compliance stakeholders to ensure technology decisions align with enterprise control requirements. Assess the operational and architectural implications of technology choices in regulated and high-availability environments. Talent and Capability Development Mentor and coach architects and senior technology professionals. Contribute to architecture capability development, communities of practice, and architecture operating model maturity. Support common role expectations, competency models, and quality standards across the architecture function. Promote enterprise-first thinking, sound decision-making, and strong architecture discipline. You Have: Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Computer Science , Information Systems, Engineering, or related field. 1 2 + years of progressive experience in enterprise architecture, solution architecture, domain architecture, or senior technology strategy roles. Deep cross-domain expertise spanning applications, integration, data, AI, cloud, security, and platform strategy. Experience supporting or leading architecture for large-scale transformation initiatives in complex enterprise environments. Experience with architecture governance, standards development, target-state planning, and strategic technology decision-making. Proven ability to influence across organizational boundaries without direct authority. Strong written, verbal, and presentation communication skills. Preferred Education and Experience Experience in insurance, financial services, healthcare, or another highly regulated industry. Experience in a federated technology organization with centralized architecture direction and distributed execution. Experience with cloud modernization, API strategies, platform engineering, data ecosystems, and enterprise integration. Familiarity with AI-enabled enterprise capabilities, automation, and emerging technology trends. Advanced degree and/or relevant certifications such as TOGAF, SAFe , AWS, Azure, GCP, or equivalent. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Strong knowledge of enterprise architecture principles, methods, and governance practices. Broad understanding of enterprise technology domains and cross-domain dependencies. Ability to develop target-state architecture and pragmatic transition approaches. Strong business acumen and ability to connect architecture decisions to business outcomes. Ability to assess tradeoffs among speed, cost, quality, risk, and strategic fit. Strong facilitation, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills. Ability to communicate effectively with executive, business, and technical audiences. Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities. Ability to operate effectively in ambiguity and lead through influence.
